sections.subheading: Software engineering that solves today's problems and scales for the future. That means architecting for performance, flexibility, and growth from day one.

children.text: We build, optimize, and migrate legacy systems without breaking them. And we maintain the systems we build: our team keeps monitoring and improving the applications we deliver after launch. That continuity matters, especially when you're running a business on the platform we built.

items.alt: Two engineers at a worktable comparing notes across their laptops, photographed in black and white through the studio's glass wall.

details.label: Backend
items: Node.js, API design, serverless vs. traditional approaches

details.label: Performance as architecture
items: Caching strategies, query optimization, image optimization

details.label: Composable frontend
items: React components in Storybook, versioned and reusable

details.label: Database architecture
items: Caching strategies that fit the data (Redis, CDN caching, ISR)

details.label: Multi-channel
items: One Sanity instance, multiple frontends (web, email, mobile, APIs)

details.label: Data migration and transformation
items: Legacy CMS to Sanity or Drupal

details.label: Testing & validation
items: Automated tests, API contracts, performance benchmarking

details.label: Database migration
items: Monolith breaking, schema redesign (Drupal + Acquia to Next.js + Sanity)

children.text: We stay involved because we built it. We monitor, improve, and optimize because products and technologies evolve every day. Keeping up with the pace of change will set your business up so you don't have to replatform every couple of years.

features.heading: You're stuck in a legacy CMS and content production is slow
features.body: We migrate to Sanity with custom workflows that actually match how your team works. Content production goes from a bottleneck to a rhythm.

features.heading: Your site slows down on the days that matter most
features.body: We treat performance as architecture, not cleanup: caching strategy, query optimization, and rendering decisions made up front. The site holds on its biggest day.

features.heading: Every integration was a one-off, and now your data lives in five places
features.body: We connect your CMS, CRM, and marketing tools through their APIs into one system of record. Your team stops re-keying data and starts trusting it.

sections.heading: Engineering that scales with your business.

migration.provisionalNote: The first service landing page (#93, re-ruled 2026-08-16: frame `2360:2879` is a standalone page under /solutions/, not the /solutions redesign the 2026-08-13 sync session took it for). Five things to settle before launch. (1) The frame authors ONE use case and duplicates it three times — uc-performance and uc-integrations are written here in the O3 voice from the old site's service pages and are unreviewed; uc-legacy is also the partner page's first use case, so the same row currently ships on two routes. (2) The Overview body's 'while agencies hand off code and move to the next project' is the banned competitor foil (the same ADR 0007 conflict partners-sanity recorded) and is rewritten without the clause. (3) The hero deck's 'that solve today's problem' is transcribed with the grammar fixed ('solves today's problems'), and three service-grid details drop what read as designer notes: 'Edge Functions specifics' → 'Edge Functions', 'Specific caching strategies' → 'Caching strategies that fit the data', 'specific stack examples (Drupal + Acquia → Next.js + Sanity)' → the example alone. (4) The frame writes the eyebrow 'CMS INTEGRATION' twice in the Custom Development column; the second covers HubSpot/Salesforce and is corrected to 'CRM integration'. (5) 'Service Grid.' is transcribed as the band heading but reads as a working title, and NOTHING LINKS HERE YET — no frame, nav item, or footer group carries a service-page link, so the route resolves but is unreachable by navigation (the ventures precedent). Cleared by a linking decision.
